slot.brief: Definite integral of an odd/function with f(a+x)=f(a−x) symmetry over a symmetric or shifted interval; use property to reduce to a standard integral.

verdicts.working: Let g(x)=sin x/(1+cos²x), which is symmetric about π/2. Thus ∫₀^π xg(x)dx=(π/2)∫₀^πg(x)dx. With u=cos x, the latter integral is ∫₋₁¹du/(1+u²)=π/2. Hence the value is π²/4.

working:
Let $f(x)=\dfrac{\sin x}{1+\cos^2x}$; then $f(\pi-x)=f(x)$, so $\int_0^\pi xf(x)\,dx=\dfrac{\pi}{2}\int_0^\pi f(x)\,dx$. Also, $\int_0^\pi f(x)\,dx=2\int_0^{\pi/2}\dfrac{\sin x}{1+\cos^2x}\,dx=2\int_0^1\dfrac{du}{1+u^2}=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$. Hence the required value is $\dfrac{\pi^2}{4}$.

Independent check: Let g(x)=sin x/(1+cos²x), which is symmetric about π/2. Thus ∫₀^π xg(x)dx=(π/2)∫₀^πg(x)dx. With u=cos x, the latter integral is ∫₋₁¹du/(1+u²)=π/2. Hence the value is π²/4.
